summary: Iteration 3 full pass — all new items green plus regression. Backend (6/6 pytest in test_iteration3.py, 20.7s): GET /api/catalogue.pdf?refresh=1 → 200 application/pdf, size ~2.4MB (in 1–4MB range), 17 pages exactly, cover page text contains 'Precision Prepress' and 'Company profile' (pymupdf extracts these with letter-spacing artifacts due to CSS uppercase+tracking; test normalizes whitespace and case), contents page text contains 'What's inside' and 'Kodak Flexcel NX'. POST /api/enquiries valid payload → 201, id retrievable via GET /api/enquiries/{id} with matching email, and backend.err.log contains the expected 'Enquiry alert skipped: RESEND_API_KEY / NOTIFY_EMAIL not configured' warning with no 'Enquiry alert failed' and no 500. Frontend (Playwright, 1920x1080): leadership-section has exactly 2 images with src '/leaders/kc-mohan.jpg' and '/leaders/k-anandhi.jpg', both loaded (naturalWidth=900>0); names 'K. C. Mohan' and 'K. Anandhi' both visible. print-cover and print-contents elements exist in DOM (count=1 each) but computed display=none on screen (visible_on_screen=False), i.e. print-only. hero-download-pdf-button triggered a real browser download named 'Sree-Bloomy-Graphics-Catalogue.pdf' (expect_download, cached path ~<3s), success toast 'Catalogue downloaded.' rendered. Enquiry form submission via consultation-form-submit-button produced enquiry-success ('Thank you. Your artwork brief is with our prepress team.') and 'Enquiry received' toast. Zero console errors and zero page errors across the full flow.
critical_code_review_comments: email_service.send_enquiry_alert uses asyncio.to_thread(resend.Emails.send) inside a BackgroundTask — good, will not block the request. However the Resend SDK exception is only logged; consider surfacing repeated failures to an ops metric so silent email outages are noticed.

pdf_service.compress_pdf converts every raster (including PNG with alpha) to RGB JPEG — any transparent logos on light backgrounds will lose their alpha channel and can appear on unexpected fills. Currently backgrounds look intentional so it's fine, but flag if a transparent brand mark is added.

PrintCover/PrintContents use `hidden print:flex` which correctly hides them on screen. The `aria-hidden="true"` is good; however inside `PrintCover` the eyebrow uses `text-[6.5vw]` on the h1 — in print media vw units resolve against the paged viewport, which is fine on Chromium's page.pdf but may render inconsistently if opened in Safari print preview.

Iteration 2's prior code-review notes still apply and are unaddressed (global asyncio.Lock across the full 17s render; logger defined after route; module-level `downloading` flag). Not regressions — just carry-over.
